ops.note:
Enumerated and assessed, with the scope corrected: the criterion names only `RunCLIExitCode`/`RunCLIExitCodeDir` callers, but all **nine** `RunCLI*` helpers shared the same `exec.CommandContext` constructor line, so a `WaitDelay` change lands on every one (~115 call sites) regardless of which helper is edited. The assessment therefore covers all nine.

**When `WaitDelay` can now fire for a caller not under a deadline.** Two paths exist. The cancellation path is unaffected in practice: `exec.CommandContext` installs a default `Cancel` that kills the process and it always fires, so `Wait` returns the usual signal `ExitError` — which is why the task's premise that ~115 callers would newly see `ErrWaitDelay` is wrong (see the premise-correction comment). The reachable path is *normal exit with a lingering descendant*: a child that exits while a descendant still holds the inherited stdout/stderr pipe previously blocked `Wait` **forever**; it now returns `exec.ErrWaitDelay` after 5s with whatever was copied.

**Effect per helper:** every one treats that as a hard error and discards output, so a command that genuinely succeeded could surface as a failure. That is strictly better than the prior behavior in every case, because the prior behavior was an unrecoverable hang — there is no caller for which blocking forever on an already-exited process is preferable.

**Reachability is low.** The plausible candidate is `git` spawning background work (`git gc --auto`, `git maintenance run --auto`); both daemonize and redirect their std fds, releasing the pipe. No `jj`, `gh`, `gt`, ripgrep, or ast-grep invocation here is known to leave a pipe-holding descendant.

**Deadline exposure:** exactly one call site (`internal/cli/lane.go`'s `gtReachable`) runs under a bounded deadline and needs the stronger guarantee; 6 more are uncancellable cleanup. That is why process-group isolation went into a separate `RunCLIProbeDir` rather than onto a shared helper — the other 114 sites get the `WaitDelay` backstop and no change to signal semantics.

Full reasoning recorded in the note "Review verdict: render probe bounding (WaitDelay + process group) for v0.39.0", which also flags that this analysis was not independently adversarially reviewed (the codex finder lane died on a weekly limit).
